title: arXiv Trending Physics — Weekly — 2026-10-16
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. The order is inferred from cross-list breadth, released data or code, publication status, and concrete results; citations are not a reliable momentum measure for papers this new.

window_details.revision_coverage_note: Recent category pages for new submissions were checked; replacement/revision listings were not fully verified.

sections.title: Identity Crisis: Untangling Mass-Ordering Artifacts from Compact-Object Pairing in Gravitational-Wave Populations
sections.abstract: The authors show how ordering binary-black-hole masses can create apparent population patterns, then apply a population model to GWTC-5 to identify a characteristic companion-mass scale near 50 solar masses.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a characteristic mass scale near 50 solar masses in GWTC-5, with the merger-rate density falling more steeply above that scale; the abstract gives 99.45% credibility against an equal or weaker high-mass decline.
sections.unique_caveat: Masses alone cannot determine which physically labeled component carries the inferred scale; this is a population-model inference, not an identification of an individual system’s formation channel.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in three physics archives; links public code; names a LIGO report number and uses GWTC-5.

sections.title: The Second Catalog of Low-Energy Fermi-LAT Sources
sections.abstract: Using 14 years of Fermi-LAT data from 20–200 MeV, the collaboration presents 2FLE, a catalog of 450 sources above a test statistic of 25, with 377 proposed counterpart associations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify 60 gamma-ray sources not previously found in gamma-ray catalogs among the 73 2FLE sources without multi-wavelength associations; 38 of those 60 are reported above 10 sigma.
sections.evidence_type: Observational catalog analysis of 14 years of Fermi Large Area Telescope data.
sections.unique_caveat: The 73 sources without multi-wavelength associations remain incompletely classified; the catalog does not by itself establish their physical source classes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted ApJ Supplement paper, long-duration Fermi data release, and catalog made available through the Fermi Science Support Center.

sections.title: A Spatial Map of the Atmospheric Limb of a Hot Jupiter
sections.abstract: Applying transmission-string mapping to WASP-17b spectra spanning 0.6–12 microns, the authors resolve morning-to-evening and equator-to-pole structure, including an approximately 650 K hotter evening limb.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer morning- and evening-limb temperatures of 858 K and 1,522 K, respectively, consistent with nightside emission and dayside eclipse-mapping measurements.
sections.evidence_type: Observational analysis of transiting-planet transmission spectra for WASP-17b using transmission-string mapping.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a detailed result for one planet; it does not establish that the same temperature pattern is typical of hot Jupiters.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports a new spatial mapping technique and quantified limb-temperature contrast; arXiv record states acceptance in Nature Astronomy.

sections.title: Conserved-charge diffusion in hot and dense QCD matter
sections.abstract: In a three-flavor Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model, the authors calculate coupled baryon-number, electric-charge, and strangeness diffusion and find temperature- and density-dependent off-diagonal transport and a crossing of baryon and strangeness mobility scales.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find temperature- and baryon-chemical-potential-dependent off-diagonal transport coefficients and a crossing of baryon and strangeness mobility scales at finite baryon chemical potential.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical/computational calculation using a three-flavor Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model and relaxation-time kinetic approach.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is model- and approximation-dependent; it is a benchmark for baryon-rich QCD matter, not a direct measurement of heavy-ion transport coefficients.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across five high-energy and nuclear-physics archives and provides a concrete coupled-transport calculation.

sections.title: TNGC-SIDM I: Evolution of massive cluster mergers under the self-interacting dark matter paradigm
sections.abstract: A pilot comparison of two cosmological cluster-merger simulations finds that self-interacting dark matter can alter halo cores, intracluster-light substructure, and plasma observables, while producing a main-halo offset from the brightest cluster galaxy of up to about 20 kpc.
sections.claimed_result: Under the tested cross-sections, the authors find a persistent offset of the main dark-matter halo from the brightest cluster galaxy, reaching about 20 kpc and lasting beyond 4 Gyr after first pericenter passage.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; magnetohydrodynamical cosmological zoom-in simulations of two TNG-Cluster mergers, compared under collisionless CDM and SIDM assumptions.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a two-system pilot with isotropic, velocity-independent self-interaction cross-sections; sample selection matters, and the simulations are not an observational detection of SIDM.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Compares CDM and SIDM in matched cosmological zoom-in simulations and identifies observable signatures for follow-up testing.
